# Volume 3 — Chapter II Garlands of Autumn

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The week that came after flew by rapidly, packed with countless “last things,” to use Nell’s phrase. Farewell visits needed to be paid and accepted, proving to be agreeable or the opposite, depending on whether the visitors and those visited shared a warm enthusiasm for Nell’s ambitions, or believed she possessed too much pride regarding her college attendance and considered it their obligation to “take her down a peg or two.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0000 }

One night, at the residence of Flossie Tulk, a send-off celebration was hosted by the B.V.I.S. to celebrate Nell and Hugh; this location was selected in part due to the spaciousness and suitability of Mr. Tulk’s dwelling, and in part due to the heavy suspicion that the Tulk sisters would refuse to participate in the event if the tender of their home was rejected. The gathering proved to be quite enjoyable, as the Tulk sisters behaved politely and neither uttered nor committed anything to disturb the peaceful atmosphere of the event—a departure from their usual behavior. Flossie exhibited an extraordinary degree of friendliness—to the extent that she went so far as to patronizingly say to Nell,
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0001 }

“That new dress of yours suits you quite well, Nell. Truthfully, it makes you look nearly pretty.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0002 }

“It is very sweet of you to speak that way,” Nell replied, her eyes twinkling. As her humor was growing stronger, the remarks that might have pained her when she was fourteen were turning into nothing more than sources of entertainment now. Flossie had a feeling that Nell was mocking her from behind those mischievous eyes; nevertheless, while they walked down the stairs, she satisfied herself by muttering to Tibby that Nell Harcourt would act even more arrogant than before now that college was in her future—just wait and see!
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0003 }

Every member of the “old crowd” had gathered, packed with glee, enthusiasm, and young vivacity. There was Isolde Pembroke, flush-cheeked and marked with dimples, closely followed by the loyal Gideon; Odette Pullen, tidy, practical, and unadorned; Opal Pettigrew, appearing at her most attractive and radiant wearing a cream silk blouse, her blonde hair adorned with red geraniums; Hugh Carrow alongside Wilfred Mott, each attempting to remain as close to the slippery Nell as they could; Carrie Mott, appearing washed-out and somber due to rumors that her father had forbidden Oliver Kimball from approaching the location; Elias Purdy MacKinnon, possessing a circular face and repulsive ears that remained precisely as circular and repulsive as always; and Barney Pullen, who occupied a corner for the entire night, let out quiet laughs whenever somebody addressed him, and observed Nell Harcourt with a joyful smile across his wide, freckle-covered face.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0004 }

Although Nell had been aware of the event in advance, she was unaware that, owing to their status as the Society’s founders, she and Hugh would receive a highly flattering “address” along with “tokens of respect”—which consisted of a fountain pen for Hugh, and a book of Shakespeare’s plays for her. The kind words contained in the address, which Elias Purdy recited using his most grave and cleric-like voice, caught her off guard and delighted her to such a degree that tears completely overwhelmed the shimmer in her large gray eyes. Having labored diligently and devotedly on behalf of the B.V.I.S., she felt deeply gratified that her hard work was so genuinely valued by the members. Furthermore, everyone was so pleasant, warm, and cheerful—the Tulk girls even displayed some good qualities; right then, Nell felt affection for everyone in the world.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0005 }

The night brought her immense pleasure, yet its conclusion ruined everything to an extent. As they consumed their supper on the verandah bathed in moonlight, Hugh committed the error once more of uttering a sentimental remark to her; consequently, Nell displayed warmth toward Wilfred Mott to discipline him, granting the man permission to escort her home. She discovered, nevertheless, that vengeance causes the greatest harm to the person attempting to deliver it. Away strolled Hugh blithely alongside Opal Pettigrew, their cheerful laughter and conversation reaching Nell as the pair lingered in the quiet, sharp air of autumn. A thoroughly wonderful time was clearly being had by them, whereas Wilfred Mott bored her dreadfully by speaking continuously without ever, even inadvertently, making a single comment deserving of attention. Distractedly uttering a periodic “yes” or “no,” Nell reflected on the beauty Opal had possessed that evening, the extreme goggliness of Wilfred’s eyes under the moon—an impression heightened compared to daytime—and how the world, for some reason, failed to be as pleasant a realm as she had deemed it earlier that night.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0006 }

“I am merely exhausted—that is what is wrong with me,” she declared, upon gratefully finding herself by herself in her private chamber. And she truly thought that was the case. Yet a particular small surge of happiness, like from a hidden, unfamiliar source, welled up inside her breast the following night, as she watched Hugh walking with long strides down through the Whispering Wood and traversing the ancient log bridge using those sure, swift paces of his. Therefore Hugh had no intention of passing this final night alongside Opal Pettigrew after all!
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0007 }

“Nell, you appear exhausted,” he remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0008 }

“I am exhausted, and, even worse, I feel discontented. My exhaustion stems from a full day of packing my trunk and doing needlework. Meanwhile, my discontent is due to six women who came by to bid me farewell, with each single one of those six contriving to utter remarks that appeared to strip all the brightness straight out of existence, rendering it just as gray and bleak and depressing as a morning in November.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0009 }

“Spiteful old cats!” was the refined remark made by Hugh.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0010 }

“Oh, no, they were not,” Nell stated earnestly. “The difficulty lies right there. Had they been malicious cats, I would not have cared. However, every one of them is a pleasant, gentle, maternal person who fondles me and whom I affection, which is the reason their statements, or insinuations, possessed such disproportionate influence over me. They made it clear to me that going to Wexcombe and attempting to earn a B.A. struck them as foolish, and I have been questioning my sanity ever since. Mrs. Peter Mott uttered a sigh and expressed her wish that my endurance would last until I finished; instantly, I envisioned myself as a despairing sufferer of nervous exhaustion when my third year ended; Mrs. Eben Duckett remarked that spending four years at Wexcombe surely required a tremendous amount of money; and every part of me felt that wasting my own funds and Thirza’s on a piece of foolishness like that was unforgivable. Mrs. Jasper Bell voiced her hope that higher education would not ruin me, the way it ruined certain individuals; and I experienced a deep conviction that the conclusion of my four years at Wexcombe would find me a completely unbearable person, believing I possessed all knowledge, while despising all things and all people located in Brierley; Mrs. Elisha Duckett mentioned her understanding that female students at Wexcombe, particularly those hailing from Portmaris, were ‘terribly fashionable and arrogant,’ predicting that I probably would not fit in well with them; and I pictured myself as an ignored, unfashionable, embarrassed rural girl, dragging my feet along the traditional corridors of Wexcombe while wearing copper-toed boots.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0011 }

Nell finished, blending a laugh together with a sigh. Because of her delicate temperament, any censure carried gravity, including the censure from people whose views she held in little regard. At that moment, existence lacked zest, and her drive had vanished similar to a blown-out flame.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0012 }

“They cannot possibly matter to you,” Hugh objected. “Their view of the world is as limited as you well know, despite those good souls being so fine. Whatever falls outside their own experience is utterly abominable to them. No girl from Brierley has attended college before you; and every pioneer, as you are aware, is deemed to suffer from lunatic insanity.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0013 }

“Oh, I am aware. Yet sensing it differs so greatly from understanding it. Every argument you might offer is echoed by my rational mind, though occasions arise where rationality exerts no influence upon me. Absurdity completely overwhelms my spirit. Honestly, once Mrs. Elisha departed, I scarcely possessed the spirit to complete my packing.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0014 }

“Nell, you are merely fatigued. Come along, put everything out of your mind and go for a stroll with me—a trek back through the forest past the marsh. I ought to have something to display to you there.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0015 }

“Ought to be! Are you unaware whether it is in that place?”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0016 }

“No. It is only because of a thing I witnessed over there during spring that I know it ought to be. Hurry. We will act as if we are a pair of youngsters once more, and we will travel whichever way the wind blows.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0017 }

They set out cheerfully. Nell, recalling the previous night's unpleasantness, treated Hugh with great kindness; and Hugh, growing wiser, made sure to act as merely a schoolboy friend once more. Mrs. Sowerby and Thirza observed them out of the kitchen window.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0018 }

“Eventually, those two will make a fine pair,” remarked Mrs. Sowerby in a tone of approval.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0019 }

Thirza flinched a little. She secretly wished that it might happen, yet hearing the subject brought up in the casual, talkative manner of Mrs. Sowerby went against her nature.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0020 }

“They are still merely youngsters,” she stated abruptly.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0021 }

Mrs. Sowerby chuckled in a friendly way.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0022 }

“Nell has reached eighteen; I had already wed by the time I was that age. We older people, Thirza, tend far too often to believe that kids remain young forever, that is the truth. Nell is now a grown woman and Hugh has become a man, and he adores the very earth beneath her feet, which is obvious to everyone. He is an excellent gentleman, and Nell could not make a finer match. I trust she will not adopt any foolish romantic ideas while at Wexcombe. I do not endorse those coeducational institutions and never have, that is the truth. I am convinced,” Mrs. Sowerby declared with gravity, “that those attending such colleges rarely accomplish much beyond flirting.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0023 }

“They have to do a bit of studying,” Thirza said, smiling.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0024 }

“Very little,” Mrs. Agatha sniffed. “Still, Nell will, in my opinion. Flirting was never her way. That said, she fails to value Hugh as highly as he deserves, and that is the truth. Oh, I understand girls! Wilfred Mott is also crazy for her, yet I would not ever suggest she wed a Mott. Naturally, the Motts are decent, trustworthy, reputable folks. Even so, when everything is considered, Motts are what they are.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0025 }

Thirza gave a nod. Though declaring that Motts were Motts could seem uninformative to a stranger, she grasped the meaning. In all villages, a family of this kind exists; while they can be upright, truthful, and esteemed folks, they are Motts and are bound to stay that way perpetually, even if they converse with the voices of humans and angels.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0026 }

Hugh and Nell, who were blissfully unaware that Mrs. Agatha was disposing of their destiny in this manner, were strolling amidst the shade of the Whispering Wood. Further off, an amber evening light bathed the harvest hills beneath a faint, high sky of pink and blue. The far-off spruce woods resembled polished bronze, casting lengthy shadows across the high pastures. Around the pair, however, a slight breeze whistled through the fir needles, carrying with it a suggestion of autumn.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0027 }

“Former recollections truly haunt these woods now,” Nell remarked, bending down to collect a bunch of ferns that frost had turned a waxy white. “I feel as though the young girls Isolde and I once were continue to play in this place, sitting beside the Nymph’s Well when twilight falls to meet with the apparitions. Did you realize that I am unable to walk up this trail at dusk without experiencing a touch of that previous dread and trembling? A single spectre we invented was particularly terrifying—a slain child’s spirit that crawled behind a person to touch their hands with icy fingers. I must admit, even now, I am unable to avoid imagining its small, stealthy paces following me whenever I arrive here after dark. Neither the White Lady, the man without a head, nor the skeletons frighten me, yet I regret ever conceiving that infant’s phantom. Thirza and Mrs. Pembroke became so furious about that incident,” Nell ended, laughing at the memory.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0028 }

Violets of distance filled the forest surrounding the marsh’s upper end, woven through with cobwebs. Beyond a stern grove of twisted spruces and a warm, sunny dale bordered by maples, the “something” that Hugh sought was discovered by them.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0029 }

“Ah, here it is,” he remarked contentedly.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0030 }

“An apple tree—and way back here!” Nell cried out with delight.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0031 }

“Indeed, a real fruit-yielding apple tree stands right here surrounded by beeches and pines, located one mile from the nearest orchard. During a visit here last spring, I discovered it covered in white flowers. Because of that, I decided to return during the autumn to check if fruit had grown. Look how full of fruit it is. They appear appetizing as well—brownish-yellow like russets, yet featuring a dark crimson blush. The majority of wild seedlings seem green and unappealing.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0032 }

“It likely originated a long time ago from a seed dropped by accident,” Nell remarked in a dreamy tone. “And look at how the courageous, resolute creature has expanded, thrived, and maintained its position in this solitary spot surrounded by strangers!”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0033 }

“A downed tree with a pillow of moss is right here. Take a seat, Nell—a forest throne can be made of it. Up I’ll go to gather a few apples. Every single one is high up—reaching toward the sun was necessary for the tree.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0034 }

The fruit turned out to be exquisite. Beneath the yellowish-brown skin lay an extraordinarily white flesh, subtly streaked with crimson; furthermore, in addition to their genuine flavor of apple, they carried a particular untamed, marvelous zest that no cultivated apple had ever held.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0035 }

“The disastrous apple from Eden could not have possessed a more uncommon taste,” remarked Nell. “However, the hour has come for us to head back. Look, three minutes in the past brought dusk, and this instant brings moonlight. What a shame that we were unable to capture the instant of change. Still, I imagine those instances are never captured.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0036 }

“Shall we return by circling the marsh and taking Linger Lane back? Has your disgruntled mood lifted at all since we set off, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0037 }

“Not I. The apples were like manna for a soul that was starving. My feeling is that Wexcombe will be dear to me and that my four years spent in that place will be wonderful.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0038 }

“And following those four years—then what?”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0039 }

“Oh, another turn in the path exists over by them,” Nell responded carelessly. “What could be past it is beyond my knowledge—and I prefer it that way. Not knowing is more pleasant.”
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0040 }

That night, Linger Lane was a beloved spot, quiet and strangely shadowy under the soft glow of the moon. Neither wanting to speak, they ambled along it together in an agreeable, friendly quiet.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0041 }

“Everything would be so pleasant and straightforward if Hugh always acted the way he did tonight,” Nell thought to herself.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0042 }

As Nell strolled forward, Hugh observed her closely. Her gentle grace and airy clothing brought to his mind the image of a white iris.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0043 }

“I ponder whether I will ever be able to gain her affection,” he meditated, feeling a sharp ache of doubt in himself.
{: #nw-v03-c02-p0044 }
